name: Rummy
description: Rummy is a classic draw-and-discard matching game. Players form melds (sets of three or four of a kind, or runs of three or more in suit) and try to dispose of all cards. Draw one, meld and lay off optionally, discard one. First to go out wins; others count deadwood points.

overview.description: Rummy is a classic draw-and-discard matching game. Players form melds (sets of three or four of a kind, or runs of three or more in suit) and try to dispose of all cards. Draw one, meld and lay off optionally, discard one. First to go out wins; others count deadwood points.

history.origins: Rummy games first appeared in the early twentieth century. Two main theories: Mexican origin from Conquian (first attested 1852), or Asian from a Mahjong-related game such as Kun P'ai. The draw-and-discard principle with melding appears in Chinese card games from the 18thâ€“19th century. The name 'rummy' may derive from British slang ('rum' = odd), Rum Poker, or the drink.
timeline: 1900s: Name 'Rummy' appears; game spreads in USA.
1910sâ€“1920s: Rummy popular in USA and UK; Gin Rummy booms during Prohibition.
Present: Indian Rummy (Paplu) and online platforms flourish.
history.cultural: A staple of home and club play. Gin Rummy was associated with Hollywood and Prohibition-era America. Indian Rummy is widely played online.
history.evolution: Basic Rummy (Straight Rummy) is the simplest form. Gin Rummy, 500 Rummy, Canasta, and Indian Rummy are major variants. Basic Rummy uses one draw, optional meld/lay-off, one discard; no requirement to meld before laying off on others in the standard rules.

setup.players: 2â€“6 (optimal 2â€“4). Deal alternates (2 players) or rotates clockwise.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Cards rank A low to K high.
setup.dealing: 1. Deal 10 (2 players), 7 (3â€“4), or 6 (5â€“6) cards each, one at a time. 2. Remaining cards form the stock. 3. One card turned face-up starts the discard pile.
setup.equipment: Deck, flat surface. Agree target score or number of deals before play.

rules.objective: Dispose of all cards in your hand by melding, laying off, and discarding. Go out first; others count deadwood (unmelded cards) as penalty points.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Draw**: Start your turn by taking one card from the stock or the top of the discard pile. 2. **Meld** (optional): Lay one or more valid combinations face upâ€”sets (3â€“4 of a rank) or runs (3+ consecutive in suit). 3. **Lay off** (optional): Add cards to your own or others' melds. 4. **Discard**: End your turn by placing one card face-up on the discard pile. If you drew from the discard, you cannot discard that same card to leave the pile unchanged. 5. **Going out**: First to meld, lay off, or discard away all cards wins the hand. Play stops immediately.
keyRules: Melds: Sets = 3â€“4 of same rank. Runs = 3+ consecutive same suit (A-2-3 valid; Q-K-A usually not unless house rule).
One meld per turn (unless house rule allows multiple).
Lay off is optional; can add to any meld on the table.
Cannot discard the same card you just took from the discard pile if that would leave the pile unchanged.
When stock runs out and next player doesn't want the discard, discard pile is turned over (unshuffled) as new stock.

strategy.basic: Prioritize runs over sets; runs are harder to block. Track discards to avoid helping opponents. Hold middle cards (5â€“9) for flexibility. Discard high deadwood early.
strategy.intermediate: Count visible cards to estimate what's left. Defensive discarding: avoid cards that complete opponents' obvious melds. Consider holding melds to limit opponents' lay-off options.
strategy.advanced: Use wild-card tactics when applicable: put down a meld with a wild, keep the natural card to reclaim it later. When trailing, play to help a player go out to catch a leader with high deadwood.
tips: Runs are more flexible than sets.
Don't meld too earlyâ€”reveals your hand.
Watch what opponents take from the discard.
Manage high cards; 10 points each in deadwood.

variations.name: Going Rummy
variations.description: If you go out in one turn without having melded or laid off before, score is doubled (or +10 bonus).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring bonus only; no engine structure change needed for this variant.

variations.name: No Lay-Off Until Meld
variations.description: You may not lay off on others' melds until you have melded at least once.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule-only variant; lay-off constraint can be enforced in rules layer.

variations.name: Ace High or Low
variations.description: Aces can be high (Q-K-A) or low (A-2-3). Aces then count 15 in deadwood.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Ace value and deadwood rule; engine constants could be added later.

variations.name: Block Rummy
variations.description: Discard pile is not reused. When stock runs out and next player doesn't want the discard, game ends. Lowest deadwood wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Stock exhaustion and win condition; overrides can be added when building.

variations.name: 500 Rummy
variations.description: Multiple cards can be taken from discard; points for melds; play to 500.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Different game; would need separate engine config and overrides.

variations.name: Gin Rummy
variations.description: Two players; knock when deadwood â‰¤10; no lay-off until knock.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Different game; would need knock and deadwood limit overrides.

scoring.description: When a player goes out, others sum the point value of cards left in hand. Number cards = face value. Aces = 1. Face cards (J,Q,K) = 10. Total is added to the winner's score. Game continues until target score or agreed deals.
scoring.winCondition: First to reach the agreed target score wins the game. Each hand: winner scores the sum of opponents' deadwood.

synthesis.shortDescription: Classic draw-and-discard game: form sets and runs, go out first, count deadwood.
